new_statements.rule_in_words: Tariang (= Ethnologue Tareng/Talieng) words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables (minor syllable + main syllable). In every transcribed sesquisyllable the stress mark stands before the final, main syllable, so word stress is final (main-syllable) stress, as expected for Bahnaric per Sidwell & Jacq 2003 ('a stressed mainsyllable is preceded by a minorsyllable'). This is a transcription-level regularity in a comparative wordlist, not a stated rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Monosyllables (tiiəŋ 'bone', saaj 'rice', plee 'fruit') carry no mark; every sesquisyllable is marked on its final syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: isolated lexical items (broad phonetic transcription of field elicitations, Ban Dak Lan, Dak Chueng district, Sekong). No connected speech, no phrase-level information. The evidence is the placement of the stress diacritic in a comparative wordlist plus the Bahnaric-wide sesquisyllable statement of Sidwell & Jacq 2003:33-34; no source gives a Tariang/Tareng-specific prose rule.
new_statements.identity_note: tare1239 'Tareng' [tgr] is a Glottolog 5.1 BOOKKEEPING entry (Ethnologue comment 'spurious'): Ethnologue's Katuic 'Tareng' of Attapeu and Bahnaric 'Talieng' [tdf] describe one language (Glottolog citing L-Thongkum 2002:104-105, Schliesinger 2003:47-49, Sidwell 2015:185). The described lect is Theraphan L-Thongkum's Tariang of Ban Dak Lan, Dak Chueng district, Sekong province = Talieng tali1257 [tdf] (which absorbed retired Kasseng [kgc]); Theraphan 1997:113 lists 'Taren, Tareng, Trieng, Tarieng' as its names. Trieng trie1243 [stg] of Vietnam may be the same language (Glottolog, Wikipedia). Any catalog entry belongs under tali1257, not tare1239; our check folder holds the same sources.

new_statements.quote: Phonological words in Bahnaric may be mono- or disyllabic, with the latter generally treated as sesquisyllablic (iambic stress). [...] The vowels in stressed and unstressed syllables differ in their phonological status. Typically only a single non-contrastive vowel, usually schwa or conditioned variant, and a reduced consonant inventory occur in unstressed syllables, while the main syllables carry the full and rather large range of contrastive vowels and consonants. [p. xxxvii] || The Ethnologue (2013) classifies Tareng and Kasseng as individual Katuic languages. However, Sidwell (n.d.) and Diffloth (1997) hold that Tareng and Kasseng should be merged and considered Bahnaric. [p. xxxvii] || Kasseng or Tareng 6b/6a kgc and tgr Sidwell recommends a four-way language merger of Kasseng/Tareng/Talieng/Trieng [index, p. lxvi]

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record for tare1239; the existing statement (L-Thongkum 2002, Table 9 stress marks before the main/final syllable of Tariang sesquisyllables, read as fixed final) matches this work's family-level 'sesquisyllabic (iambic stress)' characterisation. The work also settles identity: Tareng [tgr] is a Bahnaric language to be merged with Kasseng/Talieng/Trieng, not a separate Katuic language.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level statement only: Bahnaric phonological words are monosyllables or sesquisyllables with iambic stress, i.e. the main (final) syllable is stressed and the presyllable is an unstressed reduced syllable with a non-contrastive schwa-like vowel and a reduced consonant inventory. Nothing is said specifically about Tareng/Tariang stress; the work's own Phonetics and Phonology section (4.3) lists no Tareng/Talieng/Kasseng/Trieng item, and the only Tareng-specific entries are wordlists (Luce n.d; Miller 1988 'Trieng') and Diffloth 1991 'Tarieng (-Alak), a new branch of Bahnaric' (conference paper, no annotation).
new_statements.exceptions: none; the work adds that Bahnaric languages are not tonal but many contrast two phonation types (register), which is separate from stress
new_statements.identity_note: tare1239 is a Glottolog bookkeeping entry (Ethnologue 'spurious'): Cheeseman, Herington & Sidwell 2013 p. xxxvii and index p. lxvi state that Ethnologue's Tareng [tgr] and Kasseng [kgc] are not separate Katuic languages but Bahnaric, and that Sidwell recommends a four-way merger Kasseng/Tareng/Talieng/Trieng (tdf/stg). The real languoid is Talieng/Tariang (tali1257); L-Thongkum's data are from Ban Dak Lan, Dak Chueng district, Sekong province, Laos. Any catalog entry should be filed under tali1257 rather than tare1239.
